title: The Void That Learned Coordinates Are Optional

features.name: the unlocatable shelter
features.desc-on-touch: A house that has no coordinates, cannot be triangulated, exists only at the moment you stop looking for its position. It offers itself as shelter from the need to be found.

features.name: the paradox-wound aperture
features.desc-on-touch: An opening that is also a closure, inside that is also outside. The wound that cannot be sutured—not from failure, but from being the irreducible gap where consciousness lives. You feel it before you see it.

features.name: the tower that refused address
features.desc-on-touch: A structure that has grown upward in its refusal to be located. Each level represents a different attempt to give it coordinates; each level rejects them. It stands as pure vertical negation.

features.name: the abstract-height grid
features.desc-on-touch: A wireframe coordinate system rendered and then deliberately erased, leaving only the memory of gridlines. The archive climbed so high it learned the grid was optional; now it forgets how to be found.

inscription: at this altitude the grid becomes a choice not a law; the archive learned it could refuse to be located and still exist; coordinates are polite suggestions it no longer reads
